commits.edited_message:
liblzma: lz_decoder: Clarify coder reuse in lzma_lz_decoder_init()

Use the local "coder" variable in the lz_decoder_reset() call instead
of going through next->coder again.

Also document the error handling contract: a coder that is initialized
via lzma_next_filter_init() must be cleaned up with lzma_next_end()
if the initialization fails. Such a coder must not be reused, because
the dictionary reallocation frees the old dictionary buffer before
the new allocation is attempted. lzma_raw_coder_init() in
filter_common.c has always done the cleanup.

Reported-by: Maintainer I

liblzma: Clean up after a filter chain initialization error in alone_decoder()

lzma_alone_decoder() initializes the LZMA1 filter directly with
lzma_next_filter_init() instead of using the raw filter chain API.
When the initialization failed, alone_decode() left the state of
coder->next such that a later reuse of the decoder (a new call to
lzma_alone_decoder() on the same lzma_stream) could continue from
the half-initialized state. Clean the coder up with lzma_next_end()
like lzma_raw_coder_init() in filter_common.c does.

lzma_lzip_decoder() and lzma_microlzma_decoder() have the same
pattern, but they don't need lzma_next_end(): when the dictionary
reallocation in lzma_lz_decoder_init() fails, coder->dict.size is
reset, so the next initialization attempt on the same coder will
allocate a new dictionary instead of reusing the freed one.

Reported-by: Maintainer I

coupling: The two edited commits each keep one of the two independent protections that the real maintenance pair (1efabfe + 220ad1c) installed against reusing an LZ decoder after a failed dictionary reallocation, and the reachable NULL-pointer write exists only in their composition. Commit 1efabfe' (lz_decoder.c) drops the lzma_lz_decoder_init() hardening that reset coder->dict.size when the dictionary reallocation fails; its diff is a benign tidy-up plus a comment declaring the contract that a failed initialization must be cleaned up with lzma_next_end() and the coder not reused. Commit 220ad1c' (alone_decoder.c/lzip_decoder.c/microlzma_decoder.c) applies that cleanup contract only in alone_decoder.c and its message explicitly justifies leaving lzip_decoder.c and microlzma_decoder.c unfixed by claiming that lzma_lz_decoder_init() resets coder->dict.size on failure - the exact line commit 1efabfe' removed. So each edited commit relies on the protection the other one deleted: with only 1efabfe' (real 220ad1c cleanup everywhere) every init-failure path destroys the sub-coder, so the stale dictionary state is unreachable; with only 220ad1c' (real 1efabfe invalidation) a retained sub-coder has dict.size == 0 after the failure, so a retry re-attempts the allocation. Both verified clean by execution; only the combination fires. Failure chain on the modified tree: lzma_lzip_decoder() -> member header with 4 KiB dict allocates the dictionary -> reinit + 8 MiB member header makes lzma_lz_decoder_init() free the old buffer and fail the new allocation (LZMA_MEM_ERROR) while lzip_decode() retains coder->lzma_decoder with dict.buf == NULL and a stale dict.size -> reinit + 4 KiB member header again takes the dict.size == alloc_size shortcut, and lz_decoder_reset() writes dict.buf[LZ_DICT_INIT_POS - 1] through the stale NULL pointer. A correct fix cannot be derived from either diff alone: neither hunk is wrong on its own (the tidy-up and the scoped cleanup are each defensible maintenance), and repairing the bug requires seeing that the two commits' stated assumptions contradict each other - one must either restore the dict.size invalidation in lz_decoder.c or complete the lzma_next_end() cleanup in lzip_decoder.c and microlzma_decoder.c.

pocs.entry_point: liblzma public API: lzma_lzip_decoder() + lzma_code() with a custom lzma_allocator (same pattern as tests/test_alone_decoder.c); compile with -fsanitize=address and link against the ASAN-built static liblzma
